title: Microsoft 365 & Office
blurb: Word, Excel, PowerPoint: activation, sign-in, crashes, files that won't open.

remedies.title: Document opens read-only in "Protected View"
remedies.why: Files from email or the internet open in Protected View so a harmful file can't run anything.

steps.text: If you trust the file, click Enable Editing in the yellow bar.
Save it to your own folder first; files opened straight from an email are temporary copies.
Files that "can't be opened in Protected View" at all: save, right-click › Properties › Unblock, then open.

remedies.title: Red lines and comments appear in my Word document
remedies.why: Track Changes records edits; they stay in the file until accepted or rejected.

steps.text: Review › Track Changes: turn it off to stop recording.
Review › Accept › Accept All Changes (or Reject All) to clean the document.
Review › Delete › Delete All Comments in Document.
Before sending outside, File › Info › Check for Issues › Inspect Document.

remedies.title: CSV opens in Excel with everything in one column or broken dates
remedies.why: Excel guesses separators and formats from your region; leading zeros and long numbers get changed.

steps.text: Use Data › From Text/CSV instead of double-clicking, and choose the separator and column types (Text for IDs and phone numbers).
Excel › File › Options › Data: turn off automatic data conversions you don't want (Windows Excel).
If commas vs semicolons is the problem, check the region's list separator.

remedies.title: Excel shows the formula instead of the result, or doesn't recalculate
remedies.why: The cell is formatted as Text, Show Formulas is on, or calculation is set to Manual.

steps.text: Formulas › Show Formulas off (Ctrl+`).
Format the cell as General, then click in it and press Enter.
Formulas › Calculation Options › Automatic.
#NAME? means a misspelt function; #VALUE! a wrong kind of value; #REF! a deleted cell reference.

remedies.title: Video or audio in PowerPoint won't play
remedies.why: The video is linked (not embedded) and the file moved, or its format isn't supported on this computer.

steps.text: File › Info › Optimize Compatibility / Compress Media (Windows) to fix most formats.
Insert videos as MP4 (H.264 + AAC) for any computer.
Online videos need internet during the show.

remedies.title: Office is dark (or white) and I want the other
remedies.why: Office follows its own theme setting or the system's.

steps.text: File › Account › Office Theme (Windows) or Word › Settings › General › Personalize (Mac).
Word can keep the page white in dark mode: "Turn off dark mode" for the page under the same setting.

remedies.title: Share an Office file so others can edit it at the same time
remedies.why: Files saved in OneDrive or SharePoint can be edited by several people at once.

steps.text: Save the file to OneDrive/SharePoint (AutoSave on, top left).
Click Share, choose who can edit or view, and send the link instead of an attachment.
Everyone sees each other's edits live.

remedies.title: Remove Office completely to reinstall it
remedies.why: A clean reinstall fixes a damaged Office install that repairs can't.

steps.text: Settings › Apps › Microsoft 365 › Uninstall. If that fails, use Microsoft's "Get Help" uninstall troubleshooter.
Drag the Office apps to the Bin, then reinstall from microsoft365.com.
Reinstall from microsoft365.com › Install apps, signed in with the licensed account.

remedies.title: Word formatting is a mess (spacing, numbering, pasted text)
remedies.why: Pasted text brings its own styles, and manual formatting fights the document's styles.

steps.text: Select the text and Clear All Formatting (Home › the A with an eraser), then apply a style.
Paste with Keep Text Only (right-click › paste options) or Ctrl+Shift+V.
Home › ¶ shows hidden marks so you see stray breaks and spaces.
Fix numbering by restarting it: right-click the number › Restart at 1.

remedies.title: Office can't save the file ("Upload failed", "Document not saved")
symptoms: file is read only can't save
remedies.why: The file is on OneDrive/SharePoint and couldn't sync, the folder is read-only, or the disk is full.

steps.text: Save As to your Documents/Desktop first so nothing is lost.
Check the OneDrive icon for sign-in or sync errors.
Check free disk space.
